parsed.explanation: Visitor-facing picture: no entry/documentation obstacle, no trans-specific offence in force (repeated criminalisation bills all failed), no bathroom/facility rule, no documented police targeting of trans travellers, no custody-placement evidence. The Anti-Discrimination Act covers gender identity in goods and services — a real formal recourse, though its operation for trans people is unrecorded; hate-crime law names orientation more clearly than identity. Against that: a documented hostile climate — low and volatile support (~40% after the 2022 attack), a culture minister's public anti-LGBT statement, a rights commissioner finding human rights 'more at risk', and one lethal attack on a capital LGBT bar (a single incident, political primary target, weak rate evidence but relevant to venues a visitor would use). Restrictive gender recognition, sterilisation and marriage bars are resident-facing only, climate signals. No universal exposure and no organised targeting, but documented social hostility with thin demonstrated remedy — below the acceptance-with-working-protection tier, above the unremedied universal-exposure tier.
